topic.name: Calculating the Radius of Gyration of a Plane Lamina

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq 3 \big\}. $ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The radius of gyration $R_x$ about the $x$-axis is given by $ R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_x}{M}}, $ where $I_x$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_y$ about the $y$-axis is given by $ R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}}, $ where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by $ R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}}, $ where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

\[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A, \]

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 3\cdot2 =6.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by \[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{6}. \]

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

\begin{align*} I_x &= \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 \int_0^3 y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 \big[ xy^2 \big]_{x=0}^{x=3} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 3y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \big[ y^3 \big]_1^3 \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{M}{6} \left( 3^3 - 1^3\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \left( 27 - 1 \right) \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{M}{6} \cdot 26 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{13M}{3}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ R_x^2 = \dfrac{13}{3}\quad \Rightarrow\quad R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{13}{3}}. \]

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 3 \big\}. $ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The radius of gyration $R_x$ about the $x$-axis is given by $ R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_x}{M}}, $ where $I_x$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_y$ about the $y$-axis is given by $ R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}}, $ where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by $ R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}}, $ where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is defined as

\[ I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A, \]

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 2\cdot 3 = 6.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by \[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{6}. \]

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

\begin{align*} I_y &= \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y)\:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_0^3 \int_0^2 x^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_0^3 \left[ \dfrac13x^3 \right]_{0}^{2} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_0^3 \dfrac{1}{3}(8-0) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4M}{9} \big[ y \big]_0^3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4M}{9} \cdot 3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4M}{3}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ R_y^2 = \dfrac{4}{3}\quad \Rightarrow\quad R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{3}}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}. \]

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 2 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq 4 \big\}. $ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The radius of gyration $R_x$ about the $x$-axis is given by $ R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_x}{M}}, $ where $I_x$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_y$ about the $y$-axis is given by $ R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}}, $ where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by $ R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}}, $ where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

\[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A, \]

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 1\cdot 3 =3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by \[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{3}. \]

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

\begin{align*} I_x &= \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{3} \int_1^4 \int_2^3 y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{3} \int_1^4 \big[ xy^2 \big]_{x=2}^{x=3} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{3} \int_1^4 3y^2 - 2y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{3} \int_1^4 y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{3} \left[ \dfrac{1}{3}y^3 \right]_1^4 \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{M}{3} \left( \dfrac{1}{3}(4)^3 - \dfrac{1}{3}(1)^3\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{3} \left( \dfrac{64}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{3} \cdot 21 \\[5pt] &= 7M. \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ R_x^2 = 7 \quad \Rightarrow\quad R_x = \sqrt{7}. \]

example.title: Calculating the Radius of Gyration of a Uniform Rectangular Laminar

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq 3 \big\}. $ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The radius of gyration $R_x$ about the $x$-axis is given by $ R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_x}{M}}, $ where $I_x$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_y$ about the $y$-axis is given by $ R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}}, $ where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by $ R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}}, $ where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

\[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D \lambda(x,y) (x^2+y^2) \:\textrm{d}A, \]

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 1 \cdot 2 = 2.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by \[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{2}. \]

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the origin is

\begin{align*} I_0 &= \iint\limits_D \lambda(x,y) (x^2+y^2) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_1^3 \int_1^2 x^2 + y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_1^3 \left[ \dfrac13x^3 + xy^2 \right]_{x=1}^{x=2} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_1^3 \left(\dfrac83 + 2y^2 - \dfrac{1}{3} - y^2 \right) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_1^3 \dfrac73 + y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \left[ \dfrac73y + \dfrac13y^3 \right]_1^3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \left( 7 + 9 - \dfrac73 - \dfrac13 \right) \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{M}{2} \left( 16 - \dfrac83 \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \cdot \dfrac{40}3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{20M}{3}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ R_0^2 = \dfrac{20}{3}\quad \Rightarrow\quad R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{20}{3}}=2\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{3}}. \]

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq x \leq 4, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq 3 \big\}. $ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The radius of gyration $R_x$ about the $x$-axis is given by $ R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_x}{M}}, $ where $I_x$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_y$ about the $y$-axis is given by $ R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}}, $ where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

  • The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by $ R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}}, $ where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

\[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D \lambda(x,y) (x^2+y^2) \:\textrm{d}A, \]

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 3 \cdot2 = 6.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by \[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{6}. \]

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the origin is

\begin{align*} I_0 &= \iint\limits_D \lambda(x,y) (x^2+y^2) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 \int_1^4 x^2 + y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 \left[ \dfrac13x^3 + xy^2 \right]_{x=1}^{x=4} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 \left( \dfrac{64}{3} + 4y^2 - \dfrac{1}{3} - y^2 \right) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \int_1^3 21 + 3y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \left[ 21y + y^3 \right]_1^3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \left( 63 + 27 - 21 - 1 \right) \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{M}{6} \left( 90 - 22 \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{6} \cdot 68 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{34M}{3}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ R_0^2 = \dfrac{34}{3}\quad \Rightarrow\quad R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{34}{3}}. \]
